Keltner Channels#

Heuristic1 min read
◆ The PatternBands set by average range instead of standard deviation, so a single outlier moves them less

// Bands set by average range instead of standard deviation, so a single outlier moves them less

Keltner Channels — Chester Keltner (1960), modernized by Linda Raschke.

Middle = EMA(20)
Upper = EMA(20) + 2 × ATR(10)
Lower = EMA(20) − 2 × ATR(10)
vs. Bollinger Bands:
• Bollinger uses σ (standard deviation) → more jagged
• Keltner uses ATR → smoother channels
• TTM Squeeze: Bollinger Bands move INSIDE Keltner Channels → extreme low volatility → explosive move imminent
Worked example

Middle line EMA(5), bands two ATR(5) away. Day 15: 102.53 ± 2 × 3.41, so 95.72 to 109.35. On the same day Bollinger’s bands are 98.21 to 105.79: the ATR bands are wider, and moved less on day 13’s drop (lower band 95.55, against Bollinger’s 98.48).

Where it misleads
  • Band breaks are rarer than with Bollinger: fewer signals, and later ones.
  • Band width comes from ATR, so one gap day widens the channel for several bars.
  • Settings vary (an EMA of 20 with 2 × ATR of 10 is common; Keltner’s original used a 10-day average of the daily range), and results depend on which you pick.
In code
pc = df['close'].shift()
tr = pd.concat([df['high'] - df['low'], (df['high'] - pc).abs(), (df['low'] - pc).abs()], axis=1).max(axis=1)
atr = tr.ewm(alpha=1/5, adjust=False).mean()
mid = df['close'].ewm(span=5, adjust=False).mean()
df['kc_up'], df['kc_mid'], df['kc_lo'] = mid + 2 * atr, mid, mid - 2 * atr

Assumes import numpy as np, import pandas as pd, and a DataFrame df with columns high, low, close and volume — the 15 days above.

Sources
  • C. W. Keltner, How to Make Money in Commodities, Keltner Statistical Service, 1960
  • Trading Systems and Methods (5th ed.), P. J. Kaufman, Wiley, 2013
Pattern bridge: EMA ± ATR multiples blend trend and volatility — like confidence intervals around a moving center.
